messages:
dmitri: heads-up — after last night's release we're seeing a ~22% token/sec drop on continuous-batcher workloads for prod-live model. Queueing delays spiked and average batch size halved. attaching quick profiler dump. :eyes:

perf-bot: CI perf check failed on release/2026-03-17 — tok/sec decreased by 18% (p=0.003). Full report: https://ci.re/redwood/perf/2026-03-17/3421

amy: ugh. do we know whether this is kernel-selection, batching heuristics, or KV cache behavior? any obvious culprit in the changelog?

ryan: there was a prefetch/policy tweak in PR #3421 — changed awake_threshold and prefetch stride plus an unrelated kernel-affinity heuristic tweak. tagging @sasha who owns scheduler changes.

sasha: pulling profiler traces now. early look: continuous-batcher drain time up, P95 queue_ms jumped, and KV hitrate dropped ~7% for requests that used prefix caching. hypothesis: new prefetch stride is causing more out-of-band prefetches that prevent batch coalescing and thrash KV warmup.

dmitri: quick perf dump I ran against a representative workload:

```
perf dump --window=5m --target=continuous-batcher --fields=tok/sec,queue_ms,batch_size,kvcache_hit
# before (stable):
# tok/sec: 780
# queue_ms P95: 120
# mean batch_size: 18
# kv_hit: 0.62
# after (post-release):
# tok/sec: 610
# queue_ms P95: 420
# mean batch_size: 9
# kv_hit: 0.55
```

amy: those numbers line up with the user-facing latencies we've been seeing. can we bisect to confirm #3421? if it's that PR we should roll it back or pin old policy immediately.

ryan: started a quick bisect locally. toggling awake_threshold back to the previous value on the canary cluster improves batch_size and tok/sec in the harness (~+20% tok/sec) — so far signals point at the prefetch policy change rather than the kernel tweak. diff I used to test:

```
- awake_threshold = 0.12
- prefetch_stride = 4
+ awake_threshold = 0.08  # revert to previous
+ prefetch_stride = 2
```

sasha: good find. i'll prepare a hotfix that reverts the prefetch stride & restores the awake_threshold. will also add a guard: disable the new prefetch path when KV warmup < 70% to avoid breaking coalescing. putting rollout on HOLD now. creating rollout-blocker ticket.

release-bot: rollout put on hold for release/2026-03-18 due to perf regression (ticket RED-489).

amy: also let's add a CI regression test: run synthetic mixed-prefix workloads that measure tok/sec, mean batch size, and kv_hit over a warmup window. want this gated on PRs that touch prefetch/ctb heuristics.

dmitri: agreed — i'll add the harness and a perf-check job. @sasha please coordinate the hotfix and run the revert canary. once we confirm tok/sec returns to baseline we can roll forward with the guarded change and a gradual ramp. :thumbsup:

sasha: on it — will post canary results in this thread. thanks for the quick triage team.
